ns2:section.sectionText: Topic Section D: Teenagers and Teenpics, 1950s–2000s While young people aged 13 to 19 have existed ever since the lifespan of the human being became long enough, teenagers did not come to be a recognized demographic until the 1950s. We will explore the social and economic reasons for this development at the same time as we see how changes in attitudes toward teenagers have been represented in American films. To foreground attitudes toward teenagers, the course will be organized thematically—horror, high school, family, love, and sex—looking at each of these through emblematic films from the 1950s through the 2000s. Evaluated work will include active participation in class discussion, response papers, and three or four short essays.
